subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmeai.com>, Laura Chen <laura@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)

Hi Samir / Laura —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to capture next steps. I’ve attached a short notes file and the evaluation cases spreadsheet.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Current agent sometimes returns free-form text instead of the deterministic JSON object your downstream system expects (parsing errors and retries).
- Inconsistent schema across tool calls (search, ticket-creation, pricing API) which increases validation overhead.
- Need for auditability: request/response logs, user attribution, and retention controls for compliance reviews.

Current stack you shared:
- In-house agent orchestration calling multiple internal APIs (search, pricing, CRM)
- Post-processing layer written in Node that validates output but fails ~6% of calls requiring manual retry
- Hosted in GCP with private VPC; you have strict egress rules and KMS-managed keys

Success criteria you described:
1) >99.5% deterministic, schema-valid responses for tool-calling flows
2) Clear JSON schema definitions for each tool with examples and strict type checks
3) End-to-end audit trail accessible for 90 days (logs + user attribution)
4) <50ms median additional latency from any Redwood-inserted validation/serialization step

Proposed next steps:
- Technical workshop with Marissa (Solutions Eng) to draft a canonical JSON schema for the top 3 tool calls (search, create_ticket, get_price). I’ve cc’d Marissa.
- Redwood will provide a v1 JSON schema + deterministic output mode + example agent workflow by EOD Mon (2026-07-06).
- We’ll run a small eval using the attached "acme-eval-cases.xlsx" and share pass/fail and logs.
- Security/compliance follow-up: we’ll share SOC2 and data flow docs once we have the scope nailed.

Attachments: discovery-notes-20260701.txt, acme-eval-cases.xlsx

If that aligns, can you propose 60 minutes next week for the technical workshop (Mon-Wed preferred)?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Samir Patel <samir@acmeai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura@acmeai.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)

Thanks Jordan — very clear and helpful.

Agree with the pain points and the success criteria. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Priority: deterministic JSON output for create_ticket and get_price is higher than search (those two block downstream pipelines).
- Security: we need to confirm that any logs Redwood provides can be redacted/masked per our PII policy. Also, SOC2/pen test reports are required for our procurement.
- Volume: expect ~120k tool-calls/day (spiky at end of month) with 95th percentile latency requirements of <250ms.

I’d like Marissa to join the technical workshop and to see the v1 schema before the session. Monday 10:00am PT works for us.

Samir
Samir Patel
Engineering Manager, Platform | Acme AI
samir@acmeai.com

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)

Samir — great, Monday 10:00am PT is on my calendar. I’ve attached a first-pass "proposed-json-schema-v1.json" that Marissa and I put together; it covers create_ticket and get_price (search is intentionally minimal for v1).

Highlights of v1:
- Strict types for top-level fields and nested objects (no free-form text at root)
- Example success/failure outputs and error-codes for downstream handling
- Deterministic ordering of keys for easier diffs and validation (we’ll run serializer checks to enforce this)

I also added a short workflow in the doc that shows how Redwood’s deterministic mode would insert a validation step and write an immutable event to the audit log when a tool-call completes.

Attachment: proposed-json-schema-v1.json

Thanks Samir — looking forward to the workshop on Monday at 10:00am PT. I’ll lead the schema walkthrough and bring a short checklist:

- Draft JSON schema v1 review (create_ticket, get_price)
- Validation strategies (schema vs. runtime validators, serializer enforcement)
- Deterministic formatting: key ordering, canonical serializers, and sample diffs
- Audit/logging approach & redaction options (90-day retention / configurable)
- Quick perf targets and a lightweight load-check plan for your 120k/day profile

After the workshop I’ll produce a short technical playbook and an SOW outline for the scoped eval. Jordan — I’ll create the Drive folder and drop the schema + test harness by EOD Sunday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
